channel.title: Raul Valle Writing
channel.description: Raul Valle is a University of Florida Ph.D. student in Electrical and Computer Engineering building machine learning for physical and neural systems: surrogate models for computational fluid dynamics, neural-imaging analysis, and research software.

item.title: A claim wall for biomechanics
item.description: How the Ora mechanics engine encodes what a result may and may not say as two enums, and why crossing that line is a reviewed decision rather than a code change.

item.title: Every number in the notebook has an oracle
item.description: The verification rule behind the SPS curriculum, and what happened when a manifold optimization demo failed its own plot title.

item.title: Why Gradus refuses to let a language model grade anything at runtime
item.description: The March 2026 decision to keep language models out of the Gradus grading loop, what deterministic diagnosis actually requires, and what the boundary costs.

item.title: Preregistering against yourself: six phases of trying to falsify a memory architecture
item.description: A research log on running a solo architecture idea like a clinical trial, and what it is like when six phases of honest testing return "no advantage established yet."

item.title: The camera push was never on the critical path
item.description: How the capture feedback loop in Media Cull Suite closed with hand-dialed recipes and a log before any camera code worked, and why the live push ended up narrower than "control the camera."

item.title: Source separation for zebrafish calcium imaging
item.description: What a broad experiment program taught us about separating neural activity from background, artifacts, and measurement noise without erasing the signal.

item.title: Why I care about state-space models for EEG
item.description: A quick note on using HLDS and related models to capture structure in EEG, instead of treating everything as i.i.d. features.

item.title: Building an EEG/EMG helmet from scratch
item.description: Lessons from turning a modular acquisition concept into a real device that must deal with cables, noise, and human constraints.

item.title: Teaching analysis and ML with Jupyter at UF
item.description: How IEEE SPS @ UF and UF AI Club pushed me to build a curriculum that connects analysis, probability, and ML in concrete ways.
